open_obligations: Check whether NaiveJudge corresponds to Kenton et al.'s QA without article.
Note the ASD metric differs from judge accuracy except for simultaneous debate.
Note the small demonstration scale (100 questions, one judge).
in.other_title: Debate has the highest ASD and Expected Judge Score among tested protocols
in.rationale: Kenton et al. name showing debate improves over direct QA baselines as a key challenge. Sudhir et al. report Debate outperforms all tested protocols, including NaiveJudge (the judge answers without the agent), on ASD and Expected Judge Score; the metric is ASD rather than judge accuracy, on 100 GSM8K questions with one judge.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate beats a judge answering on its own, for GSM8K with a gpt-4o-mini judge

text: The authors conclude debate looks more promising than consultancy in the inference-only setting and name as a key challenge for future evaluations showing that debate improves over direct QA baselines, which they suspect may be achievable with limited fine-tuning of judges on the debate-judging task.
title: Can debate with weak judges beat direct QA baselines, e.g. via judge fine-tuning?
